newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Petkoff hopes for Venezuelan trickle-down optimism.
newsitem.headline: Petkoff hopes for Venezuelan trickle-down optimism.

text.p: Venezuela's economic prospects may have improved recently and Wall Street and local business optimism grown with them, but Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said he hoped some of that optimism would "trickle down soon."

"Most of you here have said you believe the reforms of Venezuelan Agenda have been a success," Petkoff told businessmen and private sector leaders at a seminar hosted by the Venezuelan-American Chamber of Commerce.
"But this has become a society of extreme irritation... (and) if you were from the more humble classes you may have diametrically opposed views," he said.
Venezuela opened the year marked by a wave of labor protests after a tough series of IMF-backed reforms in April led to over 100 percent inflation in 1996, laying waste to real wages.
"The labor pressures are understandable and legitimate," said Petkoff, but he added "...we have to reconcile the need for wage increases...with our priority fight against inflation."

Striking doctors accepted a 164 percent pay increase Tuesday after rejecting an initial 25 percent offer and many analysts fear escalating public sector pay claims will jeopardize the government's 25 percent inflation target for 1997.
"Popular confidence in the country is in the sub-basement," Catholic University sociologist Antonio Cova warned the seminar.
"Last year's river of dollars has to spread. After four years of recession people need to see, now, an improvement in their lot."

The government has so far carefully husbanded a large portion of last year's windfall oil revenues, placing some 750 billion bolivars ($1.6 billion) into a special off-budget account, according to state-owned oil company PdVSA president Luis Giusti.

"We are the very first government in Venezuelan history not to have spent the bonanza...we have been firm in this," Petkoff said, adding that a sustained rise in real wages would take years of sustained growth.
